passages.title: A parent-teacher conference
passages.text:
On Thursday evening, Hafsa went to Emre's school for a parent-teacher conference. She arrived ten minutes early and sat in the hallway with other parents. At 6:30, Emre's teacher, Mr. Harris, called her name.

'Emre is doing very well in math,' Mr. Harris said. 'He always finishes his homework, and he helps other students.' Hafsa was proud. 'But he sometimes talks too much in class,' the teacher added with a smile. 'Also, his reading is a little slow. Please read with him for fifteen minutes every night.'

Hafsa wrote this in her notebook. Then she asked, 'Can I help in the classroom?' Mr. Harris said yes. 'We need a parent for the book fair next month.' Hafsa was happy to say yes.

questions.whyTr: Mr. Harris Emre'nin matematikte çok iyi olduğunu söylüyor.

questions.q: What should Hafsa do at home?
options: Read with Emre for fifteen minutes every night
questions.whyTr: Her gece 15 dakika Emre ile okumalı.
Gelecek ay kitap fuarında yardım edecek.

passages.title: Tips from a first-year substitute
passages.text:
After six months as a substitute teacher, I have learned a few things that no training course told me. First, arrive early. If you reach the school at least thirty minutes before the first bell, you can read the plan, find the supplies and meet the neighbor teacher. Second, learn the names. I make a seating chart on my first page and write each name as the students tell me. When children hear their own name, they usually pay more attention.

Third, don't be afraid to ask for help. On my third day, a student told me he felt sick, and I didn't know the nurse's number. A teacher from the next room helped me at once. Fourth, leave a detailed note for the regular teacher. It should say what you finished, who behaved well and who needed help.

Finally, be kind to yourself. Some days will go badly. When I have a bad day, I ask myself what I can do differently next time, and I try not to repeat the same mistake.

questions.q: Why does the writer recommend arriving early?
options: To read the plan, find supplies and meet a neighbor teacher
questions.whyTr: Erken gelince plan okunur, malzemeler bulunur, komşu öğretmenle tanışılır.

questions.q: Why does the writer use a seating chart?
options: Students pay more attention when they hear their names.
questions.whyTr: İsmini duyan çocuklar daha çok dikkat ediyor.

questions.q: What happened on the writer's third day?
options: A student felt sick and she did not know the nurse's number.
questions.whyTr: Bir öğrenci hastalandı, hemşire numarasını bilmiyordu.

questions.q: What should the note for the regular teacher include?
options: What was finished, who behaved well and who needed help
A list of problems with the school
questions.whyTr: Not, bitenleri, davranışı ve yardım gereken öğrencileri içermeli.

passages.title: Is homework worth it?
passages.text:
Few topics divide parents and teachers as sharply as homework. Traditionalists argue that regular practice builds discipline and reinforces what students learn in class. Critics, however, claim that too much homework causes stress, reduces sleep and leaves little time for family or play.

Research suggests that the answer depends largely on age. For elementary students, studies have found almost no link between the amount of homework and academic success. In middle school, a modest amount, perhaps an hour a night, appears to help. In high school, the benefits grow, but only up to about two hours; beyond that, additional work seems to produce diminishing returns.

Some districts have responded by limiting homework instead of eliminating it. One school in Massachusetts, for example, introduced a 'ten-minutes-per-grade' rule: a fourth grader should have no more than forty minutes a night. Teachers there report that assignments are now more thoughtful, and parents say that evenings are calmer.

Nevertheless, educators warn against simple conclusions. Homework that is meaningful, such as reading or short projects connected to class, can be valuable, whereas repetitive worksheets often waste time. What matters, they say, is not how much homework is assigned, but why.

questions.q: What does research say about elementary students?
options: They need two hours a night.
There is almost no link between homework amount and success.
questions.whyTr: İlkokulda ödev miktarı ile başarı arasında neredeyse ilişki yok.

options: Extra work gives less and less benefit.
questions.whyTr: Diminishing returns: ek çaba giderek daha az fayda sağlar.

questions.q: What is the final message of the passage?
options: The purpose and quality of homework matter more than the amount.
questions.whyTr: Eğitimciler miktardan çok ödevin amacının ve kalitesinin önemli olduğunu söylüyor.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Hafsa, are you free on Saturday? There's a bake sale at the school.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: What time does it start?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: At 10:00, and it finishes at 2:00. I'm making cookies.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I can make baklava. Is that okay?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: That would be wonderful! Everybody will love it.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Do I need to bring money?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Only if you want to buy something. Five dollars is enough for two cookies and a coffee.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Perfect. I'll see you there.

questions.q: What time does the bake sale finish?
What does Linda say about money?
options: Hafsa needs money only if she wants to buy something.
Everyone must pay five dollars to enter.
questions.whyTr: Para sadece bir şey almak isterse gerekli.

passages.title: An interview for the substitute list

script.speaker: Mr. Adams
script.text: Thank you for coming, Hafsa. Let's begin. Why do you want to be a substitute teacher?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I enjoy working with children, and the schedule is flexible. I also hope to become a full-time teacher in the future.

script.speaker: Mr. Adams
script.text: What would you do if a student refused to follow your instructions?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I would speak to the student privately and stay calm. If that didn't work, I would call the office.

script.speaker: Mr. Adams
script.text: Good. How many days a week would you like to work?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Three or four. I'm not available on Fridays because I volunteer at my son's school.

script.speaker: Mr. Adams
script.text: That's fine. We'll contact you after we check your references.

questions.q: Why does Hafsa want to be a substitute?
options: She needs a full-time job now.
She enjoys children and likes the flexible schedule.
She wants to work at night.
questions.whyTr: Çocuklarla çalışmayı seviyor ve esnek program istiyor.

questions.q: What would Hafsa do first if a student refused instructions?
questions.whyTr: Önce öğrenciyle özel konuşur ve sakin kalır.

script.speaker: Mr. Reyes
script.text: Did you hear that the district is considering a four-day school week?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I did. Honestly, I'm not sure what to think. On one hand, longer weekends sound appealing.

script.speaker: Mr. Reyes
script.text: Right, but the school days would be about an hour longer, and young kids get exhausted.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: That's what worries me. Also, working parents would have to find childcare for the extra day off.

script.speaker: Mr. Reyes
script.text: Exactly. Some districts saved money, but I haven't seen proof that test scores improved.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: So the idea may be attractive on paper, but the benefits aren't clear yet.

script.speaker: Mr. Reyes
script.text: That's how I see it.

questions.q: What is Hafsa's attitude toward the idea?
options: Mixed: she sees both advantages and problems.
She has no opinion at all
questions.whyTr: Hem cazip yönleri hem endişeleri dile getiriyor.

questions.q: What does Mr. Reyes say about test scores?
options: He has not seen proof that they improved.
questions.whyTr: 'I haven't seen proof that test scores improved.'

writing.promptTr: Substitute teacher mülakatındaymışsın gibi yaz: Neden substitute teacher olmak istiyorsun? Zor bir sınıfla karşılaşırsan ne yaparsın (if cümleleri kullan)? Geçmişteki deneyiminden bir örnek ver. Bağlaçlar (however, as a result) ve en az bir kelime türetme (-ful, -ment, -tion vb.) kullanmaya çalış.
writing.promptEn: Imagine you are in a substitute teacher interview. Explain why you want to be a substitute teacher, what you would do if you faced a difficult class, and give an example from your past experience.
checklistTr: Neden substitute olmak istediğimi yazdım mı?
Geçmiş deneyimden bir örnek verdim mi (past simple / present perfect)?
En az iki 'would' ya da 2. tip koşul cümlem var mı?
En az iki bağlaç kullandım mı (however, as a result, although)?
Resmî ve kibar bir ton kullandım mı?
Cümleler büyük harfle başlıyor, noktayla bitiyor mu?
writing.model:
Thank you for inviting me to this interview. I would like to explain why I want to work as a substitute teacher.

I have always enjoyed working with children. In Turkey, I taught English to small groups for two years, and since I moved to the United States, I have volunteered at my son's school every week. As a result, I have learned how to stay calm and organized in a busy classroom.

If I faced a difficult class, I would first learn the students' names and explain my expectations clearly. If a student refused to follow my instructions, I would speak to him privately. However, if the problem continued, I would ask the office for support. I also keep a few extra activities in my bag in case the lesson plan is too short.

Although I do not have a teaching license yet, I am very reliable, and I am always willing to learn. I believe that a substitute teacher's most important job is to make the students feel safe and keep learning going. Thank you for your time and for considering my application.
